correctness.rationale: For geometric automorphisms, \(X=a(y)x+f(y)\), \(Y=b(y)x+g(y)\); the equations \(X^2=0\) and \(Y^m=0\) reduce to \(f^2+2xaf=0\) and \(mxb g^{m-1}=0\). Coefficient charts give the four scheme dimensions, with \(m=2\) handled separately in odd characteristic. Linearizing the same relations gives \(2xu=0\) and \(my^{m-1}v=0\), yielding the listed tangent dimensions. The characteristic-two parity split follows from \(f^2=\sum f_j^2 y^{2j}\).

value.rationale: This natural one-parameter family \(A_m=k[x,y]/(x^2,y^m)\) gives an exact characteristic boundary for smoothness and quantifies the failure by tangent excess. The parity-dependent excess in characteristic two distinguishes the family from the single-variable truncation and the known p-power exponent cases, providing a concrete deformation-theoretic benchmark for monomial algebras.
